cards.title: Install Node, Git and Shopify CLI before AI-assisted theme work
cards.summary: Set up the local toolchain (Node.js, Git, Shopify CLI) that lets Claude Code read and edit a live Shopify theme.
cards.use_when: You are preparing a machine to build or modify a Shopify theme with an AI coding agent rather than in the theme editor.
steps: Install Node.js from nodejs.org using the pre-built installer for your OS; accept defaults. On the 'Tools for native modules' screen leave the box unchecked — the presenter says it is not needed for this setup.
Install Git from git-scm.com (needed as a helper for the Shopify CLI).
Open PowerShell (Windows) or Terminal (Mac) and run npm install -g @shopify/cli@latest on a single line.
Verify with shopify version. A version number means it installed; lines of install output are normal, not errors.
Install Claude Code separately: on Windows run irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex, then restart the terminal and type claude to authenticate.
Log in with the Claude account that has the Pro subscription, since Pro is what includes Claude Code.
Verify current install URLs and commands in the official docs before running them — these interfaces change.
caveats: The presenter's exact install commands and pricing are point-in-time and should be re-verified.
Native modules were left unchecked specifically for this workflow; other Node projects may need them.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Pull the live theme locally so the AI can edit real code
cards.summary: Use shopify theme pull to copy the store's current live theme into a clean project folder, giving the AI agent read/write access to actual theme files.
cards.use_when: You are about to have an AI agent customise a Shopify theme and need the live theme files on your machine first.
steps: Exit any running Claude Code session with /exit to return to a plain terminal.
Create and enter a fresh project folder: mkdir my-store-build then cd my-store-build.
Copy your store domain from Shopify admin > Settings (top of the page).
Run shopify theme pull --store [your-store-domain] --live.
Complete the browser login prompt; the code shown in the terminal confirms you are logging into the correct device.
Wait for the 'pulled successfully' message, which means the theme is now local and editable by the agent.
caveats: Pulling --live copies the live theme; changes are made locally first and are not live until you push and publish.
The store password and account password are different things — see the preview card.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Add products and collections before generating the store
cards.summary: Seed the store with real products first so the AI designs the homepage and PDPs around actual catalog data rather than placeholders.
cards.use_when: You are starting an AI-assisted store build and need something for the design to be built around.
steps: In Shopify admin go to Products > Add product.

Draft the title and description yourself or ask a chat AI for a short, clean title and description, dragging the product image into the prompt for context; iterate with feedback if the first version misses.
Upload product photos in the Media section — own photos, AI-generated, or stock (the presenter used Pexels stock).
Set price, inventory quantity and shipping per product; enable variants (e.g. Size: S/M/L/XL) and set per-variant price, inventory and variant-specific images where relevant.
Create a manual collection (e.g. 'T-Shirts') for each product type and assign the product, optionally with a collection image, then save.
Repeat for every product; collections make the catalog easier to organise as it grows.
caveats: Category metafields and SEO fields were left at defaults in the walkthrough — not required for a first build.
Shipping is configured later at the store level, not fully per product.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Organise a local asset folder as the AI's design brief
cards.summary: Compile screenshots of desired theme sections plus your own logos, product photos and lifestyle images into one folder the AI reads as visual constraints.
cards.use_when: You are briefing an AI agent to build a homepage or theme and need it to match a specific look instead of guessing.
steps: Browse the Shopify theme store demo pages and screenshot the specific sections you like — hero, product display, collection page, product page, reviews, story — mixing and matching across themes.
Create folders for product photos, store inspiration screenshots, logo (including transparent dark and light versions), and homepage lifestyle images.
Generate a logo if needed (the presenter used Canva) and source lifestyle images from stock sites, AI generation or your own photography.
Inside your project folder run mkdir inspiration, then 'explorer .' (Windows) to open the folder and paste all assets in.
Start the agent with the project open so it can see the inspiration directory before it writes any code.
caveats: Folder structure does not have to match the presenter's exactly; the point is that every reference asset is reachable in one place.
Screenshots of third-party themes are references, not licensed assets to copy wholesale.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Prompt the AI to interview you before it builds
cards.summary: Kick off a theme build with a prompt that makes the agent explore the theme and assets, ask about brand direction, and propose a plan instead of generating everything at once.
cards.use_when: You are starting a store build or major redesign and want controlled, reviewable output rather than a single giant generation.
steps: Write an initial prompt that gives the agent a few instructions and guidelines, and swap in your real brand name (the guide's version uses a placeholder).
Let it first read the theme and the inspiration folder to understand the starting point.
Answer its questions: choose the visual direction (e.g. loud/blue-yellow inspiration vs clean and neutral matching your logo and photography), select homepage sections, and pick fonts.
Expect a plan confirmation request including your Shopify URL; approve building only the first section.
Approve command-permission prompts as they appear (choose 'yes, and don't ask again' for repeat permissions) and use plain English to correct anything that diverges.
caveats: The presenter frames this as working like a real designer — the interview step is what stops mismatched output, so do not skip to 'build the whole store'.
Approving commands blindly is risky; read what the agent is about to run.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Build the homepage section by section in plain English
cards.summary: Have the AI generate one homepage section at a time, review it in a private preview, request plain-English tweaks, then explicitly move to the next section.
cards.use_when: You are generating or redesigning a homepage and want to catch layout and content problems before they compound.
steps: Order sections deliberately, e.g. Hero, Shop by Category, Featured Products, Customer Reviews, Our Story.
After each section, refresh the local preview, judge it, and describe changes conversationally ('the icons don't match the category — quality check this section').
When the Featured Products section comes up, explicitly instruct the agent to use the real products already in the store: 'my store already has three products — use the real products.'
Approve the section verbally ('looks great') and then explicitly tell it to build the next section in the same style.
Once every section exists, run a final quality pass prompt asking it to catch anything missed and improve polish.
Optionally batch small remaining fixes (product pages, header with logo, footer with policy links, rest of the store) into one prompt.
caveats: Placeholder review names, text and images will need real replacement later.
Section prompts assume the store already has products — add them first or the featured section has nothing to reference.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Preview changes privately on a local dev server
cards.summary: Run a private local preview of the AI-built theme, using the store's Shopify-generated password, so you can review each section before anything goes public.
cards.use_when: You are iterating on theme code and need to see changes live without exposing them to customers.
steps: Pick 'local dev server' when the agent asks how to preview sections — it is a private live preview running on your machine that updates as the agent writes.
Open a second terminal, cd into the project folder, and paste the preview command the agent prints.
When asked for a store password, use the Shopify admin Online Store password (Online Store > Edit password), not your account password.
Open the resulting link in a browser and refresh after each change to see updates.
Request adjustments in plain English — e.g. ask for easing animations on load and fade-in on scroll, then refine speed and stagger timing.
caveats: This is the presenter's recommended preview mode; unpublished preview theme and static mockups were the other options offered.
After the initial easing request the presenter found the result improved but noted timing may need further refinement.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Use easing and scroll animations to soften load friction
cards.summary: Ask the agent to add entry and scroll animations so sections fade in rather than snapping onto the screen.
cards.use_when: A page feels harsh or unpolished because everything renders instantly on load.
steps: Review the first load: if all text and images appear at once, request a clean easing animation for elements as they appear.
Also request that subsequent sections fade in as the visitor scrolls.
Phrase it in plain English to the coding agent, describing the desired feel rather than the implementation.
After the change, refresh the preview and judge it; if needed, ask to tune the animation speed and stagger timing.
Confirm the effect on both desktop and mobile before moving on.
caveats: This is the presenter's taste judgement, not a measured conversion claim.
Animation is a polish step, not a substitute for content or offer quality.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Push the AI-built theme, then keep editing it in Shopify
cards.summary: Upload the finished theme to Shopify unpublised, verify it in the theme editor and on mobile, and keep using Shopify's native editor for manual changes.
cards.use_when: Your AI-assisted theme build is done and you need to review, adjust and prepare it for publishing.
steps: Tell the agent you are ready to publish to the live theme; it will return a command for your preview terminal.
In the preview terminal press Ctrl+C, paste the upload command and run it — the theme uploads to Shopify without being published.
In Shopify admin go to Online Store and click Edit theme on the uploaded theme.
Manually edit text and images by clicking sections, reorder sections by dragging them in the left panel, add sections with the plus button, and undo from the top right.
Use the mobile-phone icon in the editor to check every page and section on mobile as well as desktop, then save.
Only after manual review, publish.
caveats: Anything you change in the visual editor works the same as any other Shopify theme — building with AI does not lock you into code-only edits.
Reordering sections changes the homepage format; review after each move.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Configure shipping zones, free-shipping thresholds and taxes
cards.summary: Set up Shopify Payments, a single free-shipping zone with an order minimum and transit time, delete unwanted zones, and confirm tax regions.
cards.use_when: You are finishing back-office configuration before taking orders.
steps: In Settings > Payments, complete Shopify Payments setup so you can be paid.
In Settings > Shipping and delivery, open your shipping profile; the presenter recommends simply offering free shipping for most stores.
Delete the express option if unused, then edit the standard rate: rename to 'Free Shipping', turn on the offer-free-shipping toggle, and set the minimum order amount (e.g. $10).
Set the transit time you will actually honour (the example used 5–8 business days) and save.
For international zones, configure them deliberately or delete the zone entirely if you do not ship internationally (the example kept only US free shipping).
In Settings > Taxes and duties, confirm the Shopify tax service and the regions where you collect tax — in the example, only the US.
caveats: The $10 free-shipping minimum and 5–8 day transit are the presenter's examples, not benchmarks; choose based on your margins and carrier reality.
The presenter advises consulting a tax professional if unsure.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Generate policy pages from templates and AI, then publish
cards.summary: Fill in Refund, Privacy and Terms policies using Shopify templates, write a custom shipping policy with AI, and publish them so footer links appear.
cards.use_when: You need the legal pages that checkout and the theme footer link to before you remove the store password.
steps: In Settings > Policies, open each policy and use the Insert template option where offered.
Scan the template for placeholders — e.g. delete 'insert return address' and enter your real return address — before publishing.
Publish each policy after reviewing it.
Write your own shipping policy if no template exists, using an AI with your exact shipping rules and regions, then paste and publish.
Skip the legal notice only if it genuinely does not apply; the presenter says to consult a professional if unsure.
Recheck the store footer afterwards: the presenter's build only showed policy links once policies existed in admin.
caveats: Templates are a starting point, not legal advice.
AI-written policies should be reviewed for accuracy against your actual operations.
cards.source_name: How to Build a Full Shopify Store using AI (Claude Code).docx

cards.title: Connect a custom domain and go live
cards.summary: Replace the default myshopify.com domain with a purchased .com, then publish the theme and remove the store password.
cards.use_when: You are finalising the store for public launch.
steps: In Settings > Domains, choose Connect existing domain or Buy new domain (the example priced a .com at about $16/year).
The presenter recommends a .com for a professional store rather than staying on the Shopify subdomain long term.
Once products, theme, shipping, taxes and policies are done, go to Online Store, open the theme, click Publish and confirm.
Click Remove password to open the store to everyone.
Use View store to confirm the published theme transferred correctly.
caveats: Domain pricing is point-in-time and varies by registrar/TLD.
The presenter treats the default Shopify domain as a long-term liability for professionalism, but it works for testing.
